entities.summary:
Olympiodorus the Elder was a prominent Neoplatonist philosopher who lived in Alexandria, Egypt, during the 5th century AD. He is best known for his teachings on Aristotle and his role in shaping the philosophical landscape of the Byzantine Empire.

As a prominent intellectual, Olympiodorus's lectures were attended by a select few, including the future Neoplatonist Proclus. Proclus would later become one of the most influential philosophers of the Byzantine era, and his association with Olympiodorus cemented his place in the annals of philosophical history.

Olympiodorus's impact on the development of Neoplatonism cannot be overstated. His teachings on Aristotle, in particular, helped to establish the philosopher's works as a foundation of the Neoplatonist canon. This, in turn, had a profound impact on the intellectual landscape of the Byzantine Empire, shaping the thoughts and ideas of some of its most prominent thinkers.

Despite his significant contributions to the world of philosophy, Olympiodorus remains a somewhat enigmatic figure. Little is known about his life beyond his association with Proclus and his teachings on Aristotle. However, his legacy continues to be felt in the world of philosophy, a testament to the enduring power of his ideas.

The significance of Olympiodorus the Elder cannot be overstated. His teachings on Aristotle helped to shape the intellectual landscape of the Byzantine Empire, and his association with Proclus cemented his place in the annals of philosophical history. As such, he remains an important figure in the study of Neoplatonism and the history of philosophy.
